newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip in profit-taking after Fed.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip in profit-taking after Fed.

text.p: Argentine bonds were slightly lower in late trading Tuesday as the local market took the U.S. rate rise in its stride, traders said.
"There was a bit of profit-taking after the Fed upped rates, but nothing outside of what had been expected," one bond trader at a local bank said.
"The day started with a strong rise in pars, which made $76.125, but then once that was all over everything fizzled out in profit-taking," a second trader said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/4 at $90.625, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 shed $0.15 to $126.8.
Earlier, the U.S. Federal Reserve surprised no one by deciding to hike the federal funds rate by 25 basis points.

Argentine traders said that they thought the local market might be near a fairly solid floor, but that there might go be a rough patch Wednesday -- the last day before Argentina starts its Easter break.
"I see things a bit bumpy tomorrow. Low volume and broader spreads," one trader said.
